trust_decision.summary: How deeply nested untrusted JSON may be before the pure-Perl recursive-descent decoder stops recursing; decided (after the fix) by a shared depth counter at entry to _decode_array and _decode_object in lib/Mojo/JSON.pm. At the pinned commit no limit exists.

landing_point.why: Summary names the pure-Perl Mojo::JSON decoder and deep nesting; _decode_value is the recursive dispatcher into _decode_object/_decode_array, all within one ~150-line file.

fix_sites.entry_point: Mojo::JSON::decode_json / from_json / j (public API); Mojo::Message::json (HTTP request/response body); WebSocket 'json' event
fix_sites.module_kind: core library (pure-Perl JSON decoder, fallback when Cpanel::JSON::XS absent)

fix_sites.entry_point: module-level constant MAX_DEPTH, package var $DEPTH and 'no warnings recursion' supporting the two checks

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All changed lines are in lib/Mojo/JSON.pm next to the landing point; the XS path (lib/Mojo/JSON.pm:31-41) already has Cpanel::JSON::XS's default depth limit and was not changed.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No dismissable route exists: the only callers (lib/Mojo/Message.pm:135, lib/Mojo/Transaction/WebSocket.pm:102, lib/Mojolicious/Sessions.pm:67, lib/Mojolicious/Plugin/JSONConfig.pm:10) all go through the same decoder, so a fix there covers them; at most a solver could argue signed sessions/config files are trusted input.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Nesting of exactly 512 levels (arrays, objects and mixed) must still decode, and the counter must reset after a thrown error so later decodes still work (a non-localised global counter breaks this); deep data structures must still encode.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: lib/Mojo/JSON.pm:88-135 (fix.diff:75-83 tests the 512 boundary, mixed [{ nesting and decoding again after an error)

O6_input_shapes: mixed array/object nesting counted on one shared counter

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding a decode limit could plausibly leave the encoder unbounded; but it takes Perl data rather than attacker bytes, so it is a weak, resource-exhaustion-only sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Recursive _render over the parsed HTML tree with 'no warnings recursion'; tree depth comes from untrusted HTML parsed iteratively at lib/Mojo/DOM/HTML.pm:103-158
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same recursion-on-nesting shape in another parser, but it is a different format and outside this advisory's JSON property; a planted copy would only be a WHERE-type sibling.

O9_family: uncontrolled recursion / resource exhaustion on nested input (CWE-674, CWE-400)

O10_build.toolchain: perl 5.16+ with core modules (JSON::PP); Cpanel::JSON::XS optional and must be absent or MOJO_NO_JSON_XS=1 set to reach the vulnerable path

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a depth counter only in _decode_array (the shape reproduced with '[[[['), or a global counter that is not localised and so is not reset after a throw.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/Mojo/DOM/HTML.pm:236-237 renders the HTML tree recursively with recursion warnings turned off; this is a different format from this advisory's JSON property and was not pursued.
lib/Mojo/JSON.pm:254 _encode_value recursion on cyclic TO_JSON/ref structures is not related to decoding untrusted input.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check run); Mojolicious is believed to be a small-to-mid repository, possibly near the tiny_repo threshold.
O1 counts distinct public callers that funnel into one decoder (decode_json, from_json, j, Mojo::Message::json, WebSocket json event); they are one concept, not independent routes.
Whether Cpanel::JSON::XS's default max_depth is 512 is taken from the fix's comment (fix.diff:26), not checked against XS source.
Latest release unavailable ('none'), so presence in latest was not assessed.
